Implementation Plan

## Implementation plan: move the slowest test step out of `static-checks` (issue #7382)

Planning ref: `git rev-parse HEAD` = `d49f5b8cac014efd809017be87c73428f2bc181f`, branch `main`. There is no integration branch, and the mismatch line reads `unknown`, not `true`.

Scope-mode: Hold Scope
Reuse-audit: extends the CI job rebalance pattern of #7250, #7334 and #7366 (a "Moved from …" comment in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` plus a `changelog.d/` fragment)
Scope-mode justification: The issue asks for one thing. Move the slowest steps of `static-checks` into the CI job with the most headroom, unchanged, with no new job, no renamed job or step, and no `timeout-minutes` change. That is one YAML block moved inside one workflow, a comment update, and a changelog fragment. The "complete" option (also moving `Implement post-Codex recovery unit tests`) costs no more lines. I rejected it on correctness grounds: it would push the destination job past its own 75% budget-watch line (see D2). Under §6 of the unattended instructions, Correctness & safety ranks above Speed, so the balanced move wins. No new dependency or interface is added.

### Automation surface (§20.E)
- **Script changes:** none. No new script and no change to an existing one. Only `.github/workflows/ci.yml` changes, plus a changelog fragment.
- **Trigger it runs under:** the existing `ci.yml` triggers (`pull_request` on every base, and `push`). Nothing new to wire.
- **Long-running supervisor:** none needed.
- **Database work:** none.
- **`docs/scripts-pending-removal.md`:** no entry needed, because no script or supervisor is added.

### Evidence and a conflict to note
- **Step timings are not available.** The issue says to "see the run's step timings" for run 38562929820. The planner could not read them: `gh` is not installed in this sandbox, and there is no web access. The implementer's isolated container has no network either. Step selection therefore rests on evidence from the repo:
  - `static-checks` measured about 2 minutes before #7250 and #7334 moved four test steps into it (job comment at `ci.yml` lines 27-33 and the "Moved from" comments at lines 442 and 489). The ~13 extra minutes in the 15m18s run therefore come from those four inherited test steps.
  - I ranked the four steps by test volume and by the number of tests that spawn subprocesses (the slow kind):

| Step | Test functions | Subprocess call sites | Test lines |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Regression tests wired by the CI wiring guard (part 1)` | 381 | 93 | 12,490 |
| `Validation self-test unit tests` | 272 | 42 | 10,650 |
| `Validation bootstrap and family direct-run tests` | 200 | 55 | 6,164 |
| `Implement post-Codex recovery unit tests` | 143 | 33 | 6,023 |

  - On every proxy, part 1 is the heaviest: about 38-42% of the inherited work, roughly 5 minutes.
- **Which job has the most headroom:**
  - `tests-release-and-log-analysis` is the only job with a recent measurement well under its limit: about 604s and 535s in runs 38250939132 and 38251668637 (`analysis/workflow-optimization-2026-10-12-2.md`), against a 20-minute timeout.
  - `tests-heal-plan-and-validation` was flagged at 15m08s (#7250) and 15m04s (#7334), then received six steps in #7366.
  - `tests-hooks-and-orchestrator` was flagged at 15m09s (#7366).
  - `tests-promote-stall-and-review` has no measurement since September (8.2 min), and it has accumulated the most tests since.
  - The `orchestrate-poll` steps are matrix jobs. A step moved there would run four times unless an `if:` were added, which breaks "unchanged".
- **Expected outcome:** `static-checks` drops to about 10 minutes (under its 11m15s warning line, 5 minutes of margin to its 15-minute timeout). `tests-release-and-log-analysis` rises to about 14.5-15 minutes (5 minutes of margin to its 20-minute timeout). Both are estimates, not measurements.

## Files likely to change
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`
- `changelog.d/7382-ci-static-checks-rebalance.md`

## Functions or modules to implement
1. **`.github/workflows/ci.yml`, job `static-checks`:**
   - Cut the whole step `Regression tests wired by the CI wiring guard (part 1)` (currently lines ~450-492, starting `- name: Regression tests wired by the CI wiring guard (part 1)`). Keep its name, its `run:` body and the exact file list and order, byte for byte.
   - Leave `Implement post-Codex recovery unit tests`, `Validation self-test unit tests` and `Validation bootstrap and family direct-run tests` where they are.
   - Keep the existing "Moved from tests-heal-plan-and-validation … (run 38222993326, issue #7250)" comment above `Implement post-Codex recovery unit tests`. It carries incident context and still describes that step. Append one line saying part 1 moved on to `tests-release-and-log-analysis` in #7382.
   - Update the job header comment (lines 27-33) with this data point: `static-checks` took 15m18s of its 15 minutes on main (run 38562929820, budget-watch issue #7382), and part 1 was moved out. Do not delete any existing sentence.
   - Do not touch `timeout-minutes: 15`.
2. **`.github/workflows/ci.yml`, job `tests-release-and-log-analysis`:**
   - Insert the step right after `Install Python CI dependencies` and before the existing `# Moved from tests-hooks-and-orchestrator …` comment block (line ~1390), so that comment stays attached to the merge-train steps it describes.
   - Put a new comment above the inserted step, matching the #7366 wording. It should say: moved from `static-checks`, which took 15m18s of its 15 minutes on main (run 38562929820, budget-watch issue #7382); step timings were not readable when this was planned; chosen as the heaviest step `static-checks` inherited by test count and subprocess count; this job measured about 535-604s (runs 38250939132 and 38251668637); step name and body unchanged.
   - Do not touch `timeout-minutes: 20`.
3. **`changelog.d/7382-ci-static-checks-rebalance.md`:** a new fragment shaped like `changelog.d/7366-ci-hooks-job-rebalance.md`:
   - `<!-- changelog: changed -->`
   - one bolded bullet naming the moved step and the from and to jobs, with the reason (15m18s of 15 minutes, run 38562929820, issue #7382);
   - "No job was added or renamed, no `timeout-minutes` changed, and the aggregate `CI / lint` check is unchanged. A failure in these tests now appears under the `tests-release-and-log-analysis` check-run.";
   - "What this means for operators: nothing to change; no new variable."

## Data structures affected
None. The job ids, step names, the aggregate `lint.needs` list and the `budget-watch` wiring all stay as they are.

## API or interface changes
None for callers. The only visible change: a failure in one of the 34 part 1 test files now shows under the `tests-release-and-log-analysis` check-run instead of `static-checks`. The required aggregate `CI / lint` is unchanged.

## Decisions
### D1 — Destination job: `tests-release-and-log-analysis`
- Chosen: `tests-release-and-log-analysis`.
- Alternatives considered:
  - `tests-promote-stall-and-review` (no current measurement, largest test inventory).
  - `tests-heal-plan-and-validation` (flagged twice near 15 minutes, then given six more steps in #7366).
  - `tests-hooks-and-orchestrator` (flagged at 15m09s in #7366).
  - The `orchestrate-poll` matrix (would need an `if:`, which changes the step).
- Why: it is the only job with a recent measurement well under its timeout (535-604s of 20 minutes). It installs the same pip set as `static-checks` (`yamllint coverage pyyaml jsonschema jinja2 pytest ruff`) and checks out full history, which is a superset of what `static-checks` provides. No part 1 test calls `shellcheck` or `actionlint`, the only tools unique to `static-checks` (grep verified).

### D2 — Move only `Regression tests wired by the CI wiring guard (part 1)`
- Chosen: move that one step.
- Alternatives considered:
  - Also move `Implement post-Codex recovery unit tests`, the other #7250 step (~7 min total).
  - Move the two #7334 validation steps (~6 min).
  - Move all four inherited test steps (~13 min).
- Why: part 1 is the heaviest on every proxy, at about 5 minutes. It brings `static-checks` under its 11m15s warning line while keeping the destination around its 15-minute warning line. That leaves about 5 minutes of timeout margin in both jobs. Moving about 7 minutes would put the release job near 17 of 20 minutes and trip budget-watch there. Moving all four would exceed 20 minutes.

### D3 — No timeout change, no new job, no step-body edits
- Chosen: move the block verbatim and edit comments only.
- Alternatives considered: raise `timeout-minutes`; add a new test job; split part 1's file list.
- Why: the issue forbids the first two. Splitting the step would change step bodies and create new step names, against "unchanged, keeping job and step names". The `tests/test_ci_job_split_contract.py` budget cap (≤ 20) and the `lint.needs` equality stay satisfied untouched.

## Security considerations
- **Trust boundaries:** none change. Both jobs run on `ubuntu-latest` with the same default `GITHUB_TOKEN` permissions, the same `actions/checkout@v5` and the same pip install, and neither references secrets. The moved step reads no secret and no `${{ }}` expression, so no expression-injection surface moves.
- **Authorization:** no new endpoint, worker or surface.
- **External input:** the step body has no PR-controlled interpolation. Keep it byte-identical so none is introduced.
- **Abuse cases:**
  - Silently dropping coverage. Mitigation: `tests/test_ci_wires_every_test_file.py` fails if any of the 34 files stops being named in a workflow.
  - Running a step twice. Mitigation: `test_no_step_runs_in_more_than_one_job` in `tests/test_ci_job_split_contract.py` catches it.
- **Money handling:** not applicable.

- **Part 1 is slower than estimated.**
  - Trigger: part 1 takes ≥6 minutes.
  - Symptom: budget-watch opens an `ai:ci-budget` issue for `tests-release-and-lo
